newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says Middle East peace talks in crisis.
newsitem.headline: PLO says Middle East peace talks in crisis.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority said on Saturday that U.S.-brokered peace talks with Israel were in crisis and appealed to the international community to save Middle East peace deals.

"There is a crisis in the Israeli-Palestinian talks as a result of the Israeli insistence to reject adhering to signed agreements," the Authority said in a cabinet statement. "If the international community does not move immediately to save the peace process...then the whole region will witness explosions."

It said Israel's demand to delay by two years completion of planned troop pullbacks from the West Bank violated a 1995 interim peace deal committing Israel to withdraw from most of the occupied territory by September 1997.
"The talks are close to a dead-end after the Israeli government has revealed its true positions and intentions towards the entire peace process," the statement said.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat convened his cabinet late on Saturday after consulting with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Cairo.
King Hussein of Jordan was due to meet Arafat in Gaza on Sunday in his first trip to the territoriy since Israel seized it in the 1967 Middle East war, an aide to Arafat said.
"President Arafat will receive King Hussein in Gaza tomorrow to hold important talks on the peace process," Arafat adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah told Reuters.

U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross said on Saturday the Israeli and Palestinian sides had "basically" resolved the issue of a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from most of the West Bank town of Hebron but that other hurdles remained.
"We basically have resolved the Hebron issue," Ross told reporters in Cairo. "We have not overcome all the differences yet...we still have gaps on some of the non-Hebron issues."
Palestinians have rejected an American compromise proposal that Israel complete additional West Bank withdrawals by 1998.

"The main sticking point is not something easy. It is the nucleus of the interim agreement. It is the further redeployments," chief PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters in Cairo after holding talks with Ross and Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa.
Ross later returned to Israel for late-night talks with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

"I think the minute, the second, Mr. Netanyahu makes up his mind and gives his negotiator the green light to stick to the agreement signed in Washington...I think we will move to implement the outstanding commitments in the agreement," Erekat said.
